title: Model-sidecar observability taxonomy & dashboard sketch
content:
Purpose
This doc is a lightweight taxonomy and ops-first sketch for instrumenting model-sidecar processes and the thin host-side orchestration that wraps per-tenant inference. The goal: make a minimal, high-signal surface that operators can use to triage latency and quality regressions (model-level), cache warmness, and routing-induced fallbacks without blowing up trace/metric cardinality.

Context / problem statement
- We run a sidecar model process for private/dedicated customers and a thin multiplexer for hosted. These emit a mix of high-cardinality events (prompt hashes, tenant ids, model versions) and lower-cardinality orchestration signals (routing decs, fallback counters).
- Current instrumentation is inconsistent: some metrics are host-only, some live in model logs, spans are created inconsistently across retries. Operators have to stitch traces with logs.
- We need: taxonomy (what to emit where), compact metric definitions, trace-span anchors, and a dashboard microdash recipe that surfaces warm/cold behavior, KV cache health, and routing fallbacks.

Scope and constraints
- Target low-to-medium cardinality for time-series (tenant-aggregated, model-version) and higher-cardinality sampling for traces (percent-based).
- Preserve PII: do not emit raw prompts or user identifiers in metrics/traces. Use deterministic but reversible (via vault) session ids where necessary.
- Keep default retention/aggregation cheap (1m resolution + 13w window) and provide higher-res ephemeral probes for rollouts.

Taxonomy of sidecar events (high level)
1) Inference lifecycle events (span-level)
   - request.receive (host) : arrival time at front-door mux; low-cardinality tags: tenant, route, model_family
   - request.forward (host->sidecar) : time spent in mux queue/batching
   - model.infer.start (sidecar) : model begin; tags: model_version, quant_profile
   - model.infer.kv_hit / kv_miss (sidecar) : model-level KV cache hits for prefix tokens
   - model.infer.finish (sidecar) : latency & tokens produced
   - request.respond (host) : end time, routing outcome, fallback flag

2) Orchestration events
   - routing.decision : chosen capacity tier/zone/variant
   - fallback.trigger : if routing falls back to cheaper/compatible model
   - autoscale.event : pool scale up/down event (for Dedicated)

3) Resource events
   - gpu.memory.pressure : host-reported memory headroom buckets
   - host.cpu.swap : short-lived spike flags for contention

4) Quality signals (low-rate)
   - output.quality.flag : opaque label for downstream eval (e.g., hallucination_score>threshold) emitted by moderation/quality pipe
   - llm.retry.reason : reason for retry (timeout, rate-limited, decode-error)

Metric definitions (ops-first, canonical names)
- sidecar.requests.count : total inference requests forwarded to sidecar (unit: count, agg: sum/minutely, tags: tenant, model_family)
- sidecar.request.latency.p50/p95/p99 : latency from request.receive -> request.respond (ms, agg: quantiles)
- sidecar.kv.cache.hit_rate : kv_hits / (kv_hits + kv_misses) (percent, agg: avg, tags: model_version)
- sidecar.tokens.generated.rate : tokens emitted per-second (sum)
- sidecar.fallback.rate : fraction of requests that triggered fallback (ratio, alert if >x% sustained)
- sidecar.memory.headroom.percent : percent of GPU memory unused (gauge)
- sidecar.infer.errors.count : count by error_category (timeout, decode, oom)

Alert heuristics (starter suggestions)
- High-priority: sidecar.request.latency.p95 > 2x historical baseline for > 5m AND sidecar.fallback.rate increased by >3x in same window -> page oncall
- Medium: sidecar.kv.cache.hit_rate drop >20% sustained 10m for a model_version -> Slack ops-alert
- Low: sidecar.infer.errors.count(rate) > (baseline + 5sigma) for 15m -> ticket triage

Trace design and span anchoring
- Trace start: request.receive (host mux). Every subsequent operation should add spans that reference the same trace id. Critical span anchors: request.forward, model.infer.start, model.infer.kv_hit (annotation span), model.infer.finish, request.respond.
- Span tags (only): trace_id, tenant_hash (no raw tenant id), model_version, route, quant_profile, fallback_flag
- Sampling: default adaptive sampling: keep 5% of traces globally, 25% for traces that end with fallback_flag=true, 100% for traces that trigger errors. Additional high-signal sampling for new model versions (100% for first 12h after rollout).
- Session stitching: for multimodal/multi-call user sessions, emit session_id (hashed) at request.receive and attach to all spans; session_id is reversible by SRE with a ticket for customer debug.

Dashboard (microdash) recipe - operator home
Widgets (top row)
  - Request throughput (per-minute) by route + heatmap of p95 latency (tenant-aggregated)
  - KV cache warmth panel: hit_rate timeseries with model_version ribbon
  - Fallback & routing panel: stacked area for fallback.rate by model_family
Mid row (drill-in)
  - Error taxonomy: infer.errors.count broken down by error_category + recent examples (link to sanitized trace samples)
  - Resource pressure: GPU headroom percent histogram and host-level swap spikes
Bottom row (investigation quickcards)
  - Trace sample selector: live sampled traces matching filters (fallback true, latency>p99, errors) with quick jump to trace viewer
  - Synthetic probe status: canary probe success %es per region/model (1m resolution)
Notes on widget composition
- Keep tenant dimension collapsed by default (aggregate) to avoid exploding query cost. Offer tenant-picker with enforced query-cost warning and 1h backfill limit.
- Use quantile-timeseries for latency panels (p50/p95/p99) not raw histograms to reduce metric cardinality.
- Add annotation layer for model rollouts: when a new model_version is promoted, annotate timeline so operators can correlate jumps.

Sampling & retention strategy (practical)
- Default TS metrics: 1m resolution, 13w retention.
- Traces: keep sampled traces for 30d. Keep full traces for error/fallback traces for 90d (hot path) if storage budget allows.
- High-cardinality ephemeral probes: when running a canary experiment, enable high-cardinality tracing for that experiment window and purge after 14d.

Rollout readiness checklist (short)
- [ ] Instrument request.receive and model.infer.finish in both mux and sidecar (PR: telemetry#412)
- [ ] Add kv_hit/kvmiss counters with model_version tag
- [ ] Implement sampling rules (adaptive sampler) and test on staging for 48h
- [ ] Dashboard microdash: wire top-row panels and add rollout annotations
- [ ] Define alert thresholds and run a 72h burn-in with noisiness tune-up

Quick queries (example pseudo-SQL for metrics backend)
- cache hit rate (1m): sum(sidecar.kv_hit{model_version=~"v.*"}) by (model_version) / sum(sidecar.kv_hit + sidecar.kv_miss) by (model_version)
- fallback ratio (5m): sum(sidecar.fallback.count) / sum(sidecar.requests.count)

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide canonical name for fallback tag: "fallback.reason" vs "fallback.variant" (affects dashboard grouping).
- How to instrument prompt-length without leaking content? Proposal: emit prompt_token_count bucketed (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512).
- Rethink retention for rollout traces if storage costs explode; propose auto-rollup of non-error traces after 7d.

Notes to self
- Chat with Marco about adding a short-lived probe that simulates KV-warm and KV-cold paths (JIRA-OBS-987).
- Link to telemetry PR for sidecar tags: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412

Appendix: short glossary
- KV warmth: fraction of prefix tokens that hit model local KV cache (approx faster path)
- Fallback: routing decision that selects a different (usually cheaper or compatible) model variant than primary
- Session stitching: grouping of multi-call traces into a single session id for UX-level debugging

End of note
(Informal — will clean up into a PRD if owners agree)
